model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Both fields record this evaluating session's actual runtime identity: Opus 5 (1M context), model ID claude-opus-5[1m]. The agent definition's pinned evaluator value was deliberately NOT copied here (#1058) - the pin selects the evaluator, the record states which model actually ran. Scores are comparable only against other evaluations produced by claude-opus-5[1m].

issues_detected.description: The errata entry is internally self-contradictory: it states 'The June 2025 Data Release was published as a revision of the preceding June 2025 release', naming the same release as both the revision and the thing revised. The record's own related_datasets block shows the intended antecedent is the March 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX), since the June 2025 revision is described there as adding RGB immunofluorescent images and correcting RO-Crate metadata. The erratum_url resolves to F3TD5R (June 2025), confirming the second occurrence is the error.
issues_detected.recommendation: Correct the erratum text to 'published as a revision of the preceding March 2025 release'.

issues_detected.description: No preprocessing, cleaning, labeling, annotation or imputation documentation is present anywhere in the record, yet every modality released necessarily passed through a processing pipeline before deposit: SEC-MS and AP-MS require peptide search and quantification, perturb-seq requires alignment, guide assignment and count-matrix construction, and confocal immunofluorescence requires acquisition and export settings. The record's notes block describes the MuSIC pipeline but explicitly and correctly scopes it out as project tooling not applied to this release, which leaves the actual raw-to-deposited path undocumented rather than described.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the instrument-to-archive processing applied to each modality, or state explicitly that the archives contain unprocessed instrument output.

issues_detected.description: The publisher slot holds a dataset landing-page URL byte-identical to the page slot, rather than naming the publishing organization. The platform identity (University of Virginia Dataverse) is recoverable from the URL host and is stated in the citation, so the information is present, but the slot carries a locator where an agent identity is expected.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set publisher to 'University of Virginia Dataverse' and keep the landing-page URL in page.

issues_detected.description: Format documentation stops at the container. Every one of the ten files is recorded as format ZIP with media_type application/zip, and no slot states what formats the archives contain, nor is encoding given anywhere. A ZIP declaration is correct but carries no interoperability information: a reuser cannot tell whether the SEC-MS archive holds mzML, the perturb-seq archive holds MTX or H5AD, or the image archives hold OME-TIFF or PNG.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the inner data formats per collection alongside the ZIP container, and state character encoding for the text-based components.

issues_detected.description: The record computes total_size_bytes as 12,601,718,300 (12.6 GB) while also recording the project portal's stated data volume of 21.4 TB, a gap of roughly three orders of magnitude. This is disclosed rather than concealed: source_caveats states both figures, identifies the 21.4 TB as a project-level rather than release-level number, and states that neither was adjusted. Treated as a resolved discrepancy, not a defect.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change needed; the disclosure is the correct handling.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified is populated with identifiable_elements_present false, but the deidentification_details give a sourcing basis ('commercially available de-identified human cell lines') rather than a named method such as HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination. Semantically this is appropriate rather than deficient: with involves_human_subjects false and no participant-derived records, there is no protected health information for a formal method to act on, and the preprint quotation carried in human_subject_research.notes supplies the substantive reasoning that the data cannot be matched to a human subject with current knowledge.
issues_detected.recommendation: Optionally name the basis explicitly as source-level de-identification of commercial cell lines to distinguish it from an applied technique.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is present in the record. The variables slot is absent, is_tabular is false, and the only structural typing offered is at instance level via B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs. A reuser therefore has ontology-typed knowledge of what kind of measurement each archive holds but no data dictionary of any kind describing what is inside them.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variable or column-level descriptions for the tabular components of the SEC-MS, AP-MS and perturb-seq archives.

issues_detected.description: The anomalies, sampling_strategies and missing_data_documentation slots are all absent. The record does carry a real integration gap under known_limitations (the SEC-MS, immunofluorescence and perturb-seq modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets), and source_caveats documents a source-level discrepancy in reported protein counts, but neither location documents anomalies within the released data themselves.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record known data-level quality issues such as failed runs, dropped conditions, missing replicates or per-modality coverage holes.

semantic_insights: The DOI prefix 10.18130 is a Dataverse registrant prefix and matches the University of Virginia Dataverse landing page, the citation's stated repository and the four related-release DOIs, so identifier, publisher and platform corroborate one another.

Both grant numbers validate against NIH structure: 1OT2OD032742-01 parses as application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01, and 5U54HG012513-02 as type 5, activity U54, institute HG. Each is attributed to the correct grantor, and the record separates release-level funding from project-level funding rather than merging them.

The arithmetic is internally exact. The five collection file_count values sum to 10, matching total_file_count, and the five total_bytes values sum to 12,601,718,300, matching total_size_bytes to the byte.

Attribution discipline on borrowed facts is unusually careful. The immunofluorescence staining protocol and the 464-protein count are attributed to the October 2025 release rather than to this one, on the stated evidence that the June 2026 archives carry different MD5 checksums and are therefore different files. The superseded 563-protein reading is recorded alongside with the tier ranking that decided against it.

The human-subject determination is coherent across five independent locations: description and keywords name only cell lines and cell states, collection_mechanisms describe robotic fixation and lentiviral library work, direct_collection sets is_direct false with cell-line sourcing, sensitive_elements records no sensitive elements, and human_subject_research quotes the Dataverse fields verbatim.

Ethical oversight is documented in a form appropriate to a dataset with no human participants: two named ethics leads with ORCIDs and contact addresses, a Data Governance Committee with a named contact and an access review process, and a source_caveat distinguishing the Dataverse field label from the preprint's differently named and future-tense Data Access Committee.

Creator identifiers follow the expected minting convention. Forty-five creators are recorded, thirty-seven with ORCIDs, and the eight without are given fragment identifiers on the record's own DOI rather than fabricated or omitted, with the ORCID gap named in source_caveats.

Temporal ordering is coherent and its one apparent violation is explained: created_on 2025-02-27 precedes issued 2026-06-17, and the three immunofluorescence archives carry a later issued date of 2026-07-15 which distribution_dates states explicitly as a staged publication within the release.

The license chain is consistent end to end: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in license_and_use_terms, data_use_permission no_commercial_use, and ip_restrictions recording that commercial use requires separate negotiation with UCSD, Stanford or UCSF depending on the data package.

The record is candid about what it cannot supply. It states that the June 2026 listing carries no per-file descriptions and no protein count, that computed cell maps are absent, and that certain perturb-seq components are under pre-publication embargo, so absences are declared rather than silently left blank.

correctness_validations.doi_prefix_plausibility: valid - 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse prefix, consistent with the recorded publisher and citation
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid - 1OT2OD032742-01 and 5U54HG012513-02 both conform to NIH activity-code/institute/serial structure
correctness_validations.rrid_format: valid - RRID:CVCL_0419 (MDA-MB-468) and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 (KOLF2.1J) are well-formed Cellosaurus RRIDs
correctness_validations.url_validity: all_valid - Dataverse landing page, cm4ai.org, github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, fairscape.github.io, integrativemodeling.org, ndexbio.org and the CC licence URI are all well-formed with plausible hosts
correctness_validations.checksum_format: valid - all ten MD5 values are 32 hexadecimal characters
correctness_validations.orcid_format: valid - all recorded ORCIDs are well-formed 16-digit identifiers with valid checksum characters

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Well-formed DOI in the 10.XXXX/... pattern. The 10.18130 prefix is a Dataverse registrant prefix and corroborates the recorded University of Virginia Dataverse publisher and citation. The id is expressed as a CURIE rather than a resolver URL, matching the schema's uriorcurie expectation.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta); description enumerates Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS and immunofluorescence content across MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J cell states
sub_elements.quality_note: Roughly 900 characters of specific content. Names the four modalities, the two cell backgrounds, the treatment conditions (paclitaxel, vorinostat) and the four iPSC differentiation states, and states which modality covers which. Not boilerplate.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 30 terms including AP-MS, perturb-seq, SEC-MS, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, CRISPR/Cas9, protein-protein interaction, subcellular imaging
sub_elements.quality_note: Far exceeds the five-keyword threshold. Covers assay methods, cell lines, compounds, biological entities and programme identity, and includes abbreviation/expansion pairs (iPSC and induced pluripotent stem cell, NPC and neural progenitor cell) that improve recall.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections: five collections containing ten resources with per-file name, format, bytes, md5 and issued date
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves satisfied. The landing page is a resolvable repository URL, and the resource structure is genuinely hierarchical: collections typed as raw_data or metadata, each holding named files with checksums.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries with relationship_type values is_new_version_of, is_described_by, is_referenced_by and references
sub_elements.quality_note: Four prior CM4AI releases are linked by DOI with is_new_version_of, forming a complete version lineage back to May 2024, and each note states what that release contained. Publications are linked with distinct relationship types rather than a single generic link.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 clause by clause; ip_restrictions.restrictions records Regents of the University of California copyright with Stanford holding spatial proteomics raw image copyright
sub_elements.quality_note: Actionable rather than nominal. States who holds copyright over which data package and that commercial use requires separate negotiation with UCSD, Stanford or UCSF, which is the information a prospective commercial reuser actually needs.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No and Human Subjects: No.'; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present true with temporary pre-publication embargo on KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq data
sub_elements.quality_note: Two distinct claims are made. The regulatory line is a record that no framework applies, which is informative for a reuser but is a negative determination. The confidentiality declaration is an active constraint, naming which components are embargoed, and it is corroborated by third_party_sharing.notes.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: Dataverse landing page; notes: 'Individual file download is available; the dataset as a whole exceeds the repository's 1.9 GB ZIP download limit, and the Data Access API is offered for programmatic access.'
sub_elements.quality_note: No dedicated download_url slot is used, but the access instructions are more useful than a bare link: they warn that the 12.6 GB total exceeds the repository's bulk-download ceiling and direct the user to per-file download or the Data Access API instead.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format ZIP, media_type application/zip; each of the ten resources carries format, media_type, compression and a file_type of data_file, image_file or metadata_file
sub_elements.quality_note: Format and MIME type are stated consistently at both dataset and file level, and file_type distinguishes data from images from metadata. The container-only limitation is a reuse concern scored under Element 3 sub-element 2, not a presence failure here.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven typed links; external_resources: seven entries including MassIVE deposits, a Figshare deposit, cm4ai.org, FAIRSCAPE, cellmaps_pipeline, IMP and NDEx, each flagged archival true or false
sub_elements.quality_note: The archival flag is used discriminatingly, marking the MassIVE and Figshare deposits as archival and the tooling and portal links as not, which tells a reuser which links are durable evidence and which are living resources.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met on three independent grounds: distribution_formats is populated with ZIP and application/zip, page resolves to a public Dataverse landing page with per-file access, and the licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/'; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, versioned, URI-identified public licence with its share, adapt, attribution, non-commercial and share-alike terms enumerated. The permission enum agrees with the licence text, and the commercial-use carve-out is stated with the negotiating parties named.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1: distribution_formats populated, accessible landing page, reuse-permitting licence.
sub_elements.evidence: format: ZIP and media_type: application/zip on all ten resources; encoding absent throughout
sub_elements.quality_note: Format documentation never passes the container boundary. ZIP is a standard archive format with a correct IANA media type, but it conveys nothing about the interoperability of the contents: a reuser cannot determine whether the mass-spectrometry archives hold mzML or vendor formats, whether the perturb-seq archive holds MTX, H5AD or FASTQ, or whether the 12.6 GB of images are OME-TIFF or PNG. Character encoding is stated nowhere. This is insufficient to support integration with other datasets, which is the stated purpose of the sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at two levels, the packaging standard for the data (RO-Crate, an established community standard for research object packaging) and the metadata schema for this record itself. Ontology conformance is additionally demonstrated in practice through Bridge2AI substrate and topic CURIEs on the instances.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: absent from the record
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable-level metadata of any kind. The nearest content is the instances block, which types three measurement kinds with ontology CURIEs, but that describes what the archives are rather than what fields they contain. No identifiers, no descriptions, no data dictionary.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four entries with use_category and usage_notes; prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making and patient care, with prohibition_reason citing absent regulatory oversight and laboratory cell-line derivation; discouraged_uses: use as a source of computed cell maps
sub_elements.quality_note: All three arms of the guidance are present and the reasoning is specific rather than generic. The discouraged use is particularly well judged: it warns that the release contains no predicted cell maps, which is precisely the misuse a reader of the CM4AI project description would be most likely to attempt.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Resolved per sub-element, not once for the element (#1060). Sub-elements 1 and 2 carry the governance disjunct and are gated on human subjects OR governance restrictions; sub-elements 3, 4 and 5 ask about participants and are gated on human subjects alone. The two groups resolve differently here, which is the case the per-sub-element rule exists to handle.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subject disjunct NOT met: description and keywords name only cell lines, cell states, compounds and assays, with no participant, patient or clinical-research term; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes robotic fixation, lentiviral library construction and a 10x Genomics kit, no recruitment. Governance disjunct MET on E2 and E6 evidence external to Element 4: confidential_elements records confidential_elements_present true with a temporary pre-publication embargo on named perturb-seq components, an active constraint rather than a record that none applies; ip_restrictions requires separate commercial licence negotiation with UCSD, Stanford or UCSF; data_governance names a Data Governance Committee with a contact and an access_review_process. regulatory_restrictions alone would NOT have satisfied this, since 'FDA Regulated: No and Human Subjects: No' is a record that no restriction applies and #1060 forbids reading that as a constraint. The material is also donor-derived (raw_data_sources names a patient-derived tumour line and a healthy-donor iPSC line), which the rubric names explicitly as a case where ethical oversight applies without human participants.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries naming ethics leads Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153), each described as supervising ethical matters relating to dataset preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access; data_governance.committee_name: Data Governance Committee, with committee_contact Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486) and an access_review_process
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is documented in the form appropriate to this dataset rather than in a form borrowed from human-subjects research. There is no IRB approval number, and correctly so, since involves_human_subjects is false and no IRB reviewed this work. What is present instead is actionable: two named, identified ethics leads with working contact addresses, a governance committee with a named contact, a described access review process, and a stewardship role statement covering the openness-versus-intellectual-property balance. The record also carries a source_caveat distinguishing the Dataverse field label 'Data Governance Committee' from the preprint's unnamed and future-tense 'Data Access Committee', which is exactly the kind of precision that separates documented oversight from asserted oversight.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same resolution as sub-element 1: human-subject disjunct not met via E1 description and keywords or E8 collection_mechanisms, governance disjunct met via E2 confidential_elements embargo, ip_restrictions commercial-licence constraint, and the data_governance access review process, with donor-derived cell-line material recorded in raw_data_sources. Element 4's own is_deidentified field was not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified: identifiable_elements_present false, deidentification_details 'Samples are recorded as de-identified. Data were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines; the underlying cell lines are described as ethically sourced.'; human_subject_research.notes: 'considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'
sub_elements.quality_note: The basis for de-identification is stated and is semantically correct for the data type. No formal standard such as Safe Harbor or Expert Determination is named, and none applies: these are commercial and repository-sourced cell lines carrying no protected health information for a technique to strip. What is offered in its place is the substantive reasoning behind an expert-determination-style claim, that the material cannot be matched to a human subject with current knowledge, attributed to its source. The two cell lines are separately identified by Cellosaurus RRID with their provenance stated, so a reuser can independently verify the de-identification status of the source material.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Gated on the human-subject condition alone, which is not met. description and keywords contain no participant, patient or clinical-research reference, naming only cell lines, differentiation states, compounds and assay platforms; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes automated fixation on a pipetting robot, CRISPR lentiviral library design and 10x Genomics single-cell kits, with no participant recruitment. Per #1060 the governance structures present here, the Data Governance Committee, the embargo and the ethics contacts, are explicitly NOT a participant signal and do not reach this sub-element. Element 4's own participant_privacy field was not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk absent; the dataset has no participants whose privacy could be protected
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. There are no participants in this dataset, so there is nothing for participant privacy protections or a re-identification risk assessment to describe. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter, laboratory cell lines rather than people, instead of the quality of its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Gated on the human-subject condition alone, which is not met, on the same E1 and E8 evidence as sub-element 3. direct_collection independently records is_direct false with the explanation that data were generated from commercially available and repository-sourced cell lines and not collected directly from human subjects. Governance structures do not reach this sub-element per #1060. Element 4's own informed_consent field was not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent absent; no participants were enrolled, so no consent procedure exists for this dataset to describe
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Consent for the original derivation of the MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J lines was obtained by the source institutions long before this dataset and is a property of those lines, not of this release.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Gated on the human-subject condition alone, which is not met, on the same E1 and E8 evidence as sub-elements 3 and 4. Governance structures do not reach this sub-element per #1060. Element 4's own at_risk_populations and participant_compensation fields were not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation absent; no population was enrolled and no one was compensated for participation
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The subpopulations this dataset does have are cell lines and differentiation states, which the record states explicitly under subpopulations.identification, and those carry no vulnerability or compensation dimension.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations[0].identification: 'Subpopulations in this dataset are cell lines and differentiation states rather than human demographic groups: MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat) and KOLF2.1J iPSCs (undifferentiated, neural progenitor cells, neurons, cardiomyocytes).'; subsets: two entries with is_subpopulation true
sub_elements.quality_note: The record reinterprets a human-demographics slot correctly for a cell-line dataset and says so explicitly rather than leaving it blank or filling it with participant language. The distribution field then states which modality covers which cell state, so a reuser can see that AP-MS covers treated MDA-MB-468 only and immunofluorescence covers MDA-MB-468 only.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10; total_size_bytes: 12601718300; per-collection file_count values of 2, 3, 2, 2 and 1 with total_bytes; per-file bytes on all ten resources; subsets carry is_data_split false
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are reported at file and collection level, are exact, sum correctly to the dataset totals, and are accompanied by a source_caveat stating that they are the record's own computation from rounded per-file figures rather than a number any source reports. The dataset-split flag is present and set false on both subsets. The gap is at instance level: the instances block names three measurement types with no counts of images, interactions or cells, and the record states that the June 2026 listing carries no protein count. Reported honestly, but a reuser cannot size the data in scientific units.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false present; variables absent
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the flag is satisfied. There is no data dictionary, no column or field description and no variable identifier anywhere in the record. The false tabular flag is accurate for image archives but does not excuse the SEC-MS, AP-MS and perturb-seq components, which are tabular in substance and receive no field-level description.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances: three entries with data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:26 and B2AI_TOPIC:34, data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 and B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63, each with descriptive notes
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are given as resolvable Bridge2AI ontology CURIEs rather than free text, which makes them machine-comparable across the programme. The accompanying notes describe the biological content concretely, including the four-channel immunofluorescence staining scheme, and the imaging note carries its attribution caveat to the October 2025 release.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies, sampling_strategies and missing_data_documentation all absent
sub_elements.quality_note: None of the three named fields is populated. Adjacent content exists but sits elsewhere and answers a different question: known_limitations records that the three modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets, and source_caveats records a disagreement between source releases over the imaged protein count. Neither documents anomalies, sampling design or missing-data patterns within the released data.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, public Dataverse landing page with per-file access, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence permitting reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'
sub_elements.quality_note: The version is stated, quoted so it survives as a string rather than degrading to a float, and agrees with the V2 in the citation. The Beta status is carried alongside, which is material given that the release is explicitly interim.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.versions_available lists May 2024 (doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5), March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, version 1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, version 2.1), October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, version 2.1) and June 2026 (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, version 2.0); latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Every prior release is individually addressable by DOI with its Dataverse major version and internal version number, so a user can retrieve any historical state directly. The latest_version_doi agrees with the record's own doi.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: errata[0]: revision adding RGB immunofluorescent images, correcting RO-Crate metadata and changing naming conventions, with erratum_url to the F3TD5R release; related_datasets notes state what each prior release contained and how it differed
sub_elements.quality_note: Substantive change information is present and points at a resolvable URL. The entry contains a factual slip flagged in issues_detected: it names the June 2025 release as a revision of 'the preceding June 2025 release' where the record's own related_datasets show the antecedent is March 2025. The substance of the change description is correct and useful, so the sub-element passes, but the sentence needs correcting.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: quarterly; updates.update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a cadence and an end date are given, so a reuser knows how often to re-check and when the series will stop. The November 2026 end date is consistent with the NIH project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 recorded under funders, allowing for a closeout interval.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) with derivation from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, available from ATCC; KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) derived from a healthy male Northern European donor, available from HipSci under MTA; related_datasets chains four prior releases by is_new_version_of; retention_limit records long-term preservation in the UVA Dataverse
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance runs in both directions. Upstream, both source cell lines are identified by Cellosaurus RRID with their biological origin and the terms on which a third party can obtain them, so the material chain is independently verifiable. Downstream, the version lineage back to May 2024 and the preservation commitment establish where the data came from and how long it will remain. was_derived_from and release_notes are unused, but the substance those slots would carry is present.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four responses covering AI-ready hierarchical cell-architecture maps, spatiotemporal cell mapping toward interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, ethical AI-ready datasets, and stimulating research in visible machine learning; addressing_gaps: two responses on the black-box problem in genomics and on the uncharted state of cell structure
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the gap it addresses are documented separately and both are specific. The black-box framing states the scientific deficiency precisely, that models predict phenotype from genotype without capturing the mechanism, and connects it to what the dataset supplies.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: AI model training on functional genomics data; cellular process analysis; analysis of cell architectural changes under disease processes, treatments or genetic perturbations; bioinformatics analysis of individual modality datasets, noted as what the current release is most suitable for
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct tasks, and the fourth is qualified by what this release can actually support rather than by project ambition, which aligns it with the discouraged use warning that computed cell maps are absent.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health twice (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI programme; Bridge2AI Bridge Center award) and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia
sub_elements.quality_note: Three funders with grantor names and mechanism context. The record distinguishes funding recorded on the release itself from project-level funding acknowledged only in the preprint, and says so in the notes of each entry, so a reader can tell what this specific release was funded by.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grants[0].grant_number: 1OT2OD032742-01, with NIH RePORTER application ID 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2, FY2025 award 5289382 and project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31; funders[1].grants[0].grant_number: 5U54HG012513-02
sub_elements.quality_note: Both award numbers validate against NIH structure. 1OT2OD032742-01 parses as application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01, which is the expected form for a Common Fund Other Transaction award. 5U54HG012513-02 parses as type 5, activity U54, institute HG. The first entry goes further and supplies RePORTER corroboration with the application ID and project period.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: 45 entries, 37 with ORCID identifiers and all with affiliations; Trey Ideker additionally carries a principal_investigator block; maintainers names a programme manager, website support and the Dataverse depositor with contact addresses
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is thorough and identified rather than nominal. The eight creators lacking ORCIDs receive fragment identifiers minted on the record's own DOI instead of being dropped or given fabricated identifiers, and source_caveats names the ORCID gap. A conflict over one author's affiliation between the preprint and the Dataverse citation is resolved by stated source ranking and disclosed.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified: acquisition_methods carries four entries and collection_mechanisms three. Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, public Dataverse landing page, reuse-permitting licence. Both halves of the compound condition satisfied.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: automated fixation and permeabilization on a pipetting robot for MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 lines; a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, with inducible dCas9 lines generated and characterized; single-cell CRISPR screens using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit; data_collectors names the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and the Krogan laboratory at UCSF with their modalities
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific enough to be actionable. Named platform (10x Genomics 3'HT), a stated library design parameter (6 guide RNAs per gene targeting chromatin factors), the automation approach, and which laboratory generated which modality. Not a generic 'data were collected at multiple sites' statement.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same compound condition as sub-element 1: collection identified through populated acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms, datasets shared through distribution_formats, landing page and licence.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: AP-MS on endogenously tagged cell lines; proteome-wide SEC-MS; ICC-IF using Human Protein Atlas antibodies with high-resolution confocal microscopy; single-cell CRISPRi perturbation screens, all four with was_directly_observed true; raw_data_sources identifies both source cell lines by RRID with access terms
sub_elements.quality_note: Each of the four modalities names its technique and a distinguishing methodological detail: endogenous tagging for AP-MS, proteome-wide scope for SEC-MS, Human Protein Atlas antibodies for the imaging. The was_directly_observed flag is set consistently, and the upstream material is identified by RRID so a reuser can obtain the same lines.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software-tools condition met via external_resources (E10), which references a code repository at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, alongside FAIRSCAPE at fairscape.github.io under the MIT License and the Integrative Modeling Platform. Element 8's own preprocessing and software fields were not used to establish applicability.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols all absent
sub_elements.quality_note: Every named field is empty and no processing is described anywhere else in the record for the data actually released. The notes block describes the MuSIC pipeline in detail, node2vec embedding of interaction networks, deep-learning embedding of images, contrastive co-embedding, multi-resolution community detection and ontology-based annotation, but then correctly scopes it out, stating that computed cell maps are not in this release and those stages describe project tooling and planned future releases. The honesty is right, but it leaves the actual instrument-to-archive path undocumented for four modalities that all require substantial processing before deposit.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same software-tools condition as sub-element 3, established from E10 external_resources naming a GitHub code repository and two further tool distributions, not from Element 8's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: Cell Mapping Toolkit (MuSIC pipeline) at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/; FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework at https://fairscape.github.io under the MIT License with tutorial and installation instructions; Integrative Modeling Platform at http://integrativemodeling.org; NDEx at https://ndexbio.org; collection_mechanisms names the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit; notes names node2vec and a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated software_and_tools slot is unused, but the substance the sub-element asks for is present and actionable: named tools, a GitHub repository, separate documentation URLs, and a stated licence for FAIRSCAPE. Two qualifications keep this from being a strong pass. No version is given for any tool, and the record itself states that the pipeline tools were not applied to this release, so they document the project's software ecosystem rather than this dataset's processing.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, public Dataverse landing page with per-file access, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence permitting reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: seven entries with archival flags, including MassIVE deposits for the SEC-MS and AP-MS components and a Figshare deposit for the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas; conforms_to: RO-Crate; related_datasets links the CM4AI preprint (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), the perturbation atlas preprint (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, PMC11580897) and a Nature paper (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3)
sub_elements.quality_note: Three publications are linked by DOI with distinct relationship types and one carries a PMCID. The domain-repository deposits are the strongest element: MassIVE for mass spectrometry and Figshare for the perturbation atlas are the venues a specialist would look in, and marking them archival tells a reuser they are durable. The RO-Crate conformance names an established packaging standard.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: four typed entries covering scope (interim release, no predicted cell maps), methodology (analysis requires domain expertise), integration (SEC-MS, IF and perturb-seq interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets) and coverage (data not in final form, some datasets embargoed)
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct limitations, each with a limitation_type drawn from a controlled vocabulary and a description that states a real constraint rather than a disclaimer. The integration limitation is the most valuable: incomplete protein overlap across modalities is precisely what would defeat a naive multi-modal integration attempt, and it is stated plainly.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases[0]: bias_type representation_bias, description 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The bias is typed against the standard taxonomy rather than left as free text, and the category chosen is the correct one for the concern described. The substance is the right concern for this data type: two cell lines, one from a single breast cancer patient and one from a single Northern European donor, cannot represent population-level biological variation, which directly limits the generalisability of any model trained on them. The gap is breadth. Only one bias is recorded, and future_use_impacts is absent, so no anticipated downstream social impact is stated.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies absent from the record
sub_elements.quality_note: The named field is empty and nothing elsewhere fills its role. source_caveats documents discrepancies between source documents, the 563 versus 464 protein count across releases and the 12.6 GB versus 21.4 TB volume disagreement, but those are provenance conflicts in the documentation rather than anomalies in the released data. No outliers, failed runs, batch effects or quality-control results are reported for any of the four modalities.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements[0]: sensitive_elements_present false, with sensitivity_details 'The release records no human subjects and de-identified samples; data were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines.'; confidential_elements[0]: confidential_elements_present true, naming the embargoed perturb-seq components
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a reasoned negative determination on sensitivity and a positive declaration on confidentiality. The negative is not a blank: it states the grounds and cites the release's own recorded fields, so a reader can check the reasoning. The confidentiality entry names which specific components are embargoed, which is corroborated by third_party_sharing and by the coverage limitation. content_warnings is absent and appropriately so for laboratory cell-line data.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries naming Vardit Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon as ethics leads with ORCIDs and contact emails, describing supervision of ethical matters relating to dataset preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access
sub_elements.quality_note: The review arrangement is documented with identified, contactable individuals and a stated scope of oversight, which is the substance of the sub-element. No conflict-of-interest declaration is present, which is the one gap. Supporting governance detail sits in data_governance, including the openness-versus-intellectual-property balance and the commercialisation monitoring role, which is the nearest the record comes to addressing competing interests.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, public Dataverse landing page with per-file access and a Data Access API, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence permitting reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; citation names 'University of Virginia Dataverse'; DOI prefix 10.18130 is the corresponding Dataverse registrant prefix
sub_elements.quality_note: The platform is a recognised institutional Dataverse instance, and its identity is corroborated three ways, by the URL host, by the citation text and by the DOI prefix. The slot carries a dataset landing-page URL byte-identical to the page slot rather than a publisher name, which is a semantic mismatch flagged in issues_detected but does not obscure which platform published the data.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified: related_datasets carries three publication DOIs, the CM4AI preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 with relationship is_described_by, the perturbation atlas preprint doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 with a PMCID, and doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3. Datasets shared condition met as above. Both halves of the compound condition satisfied.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full author list, year 2026, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, repository 'University of Virginia Dataverse', version V2; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete Dataverse-format citation carrying every element needed for cross-referencing, including the version designator, and the author list matches the creators block. The licence terms separately instruct that publications referencing the data should cite both the related publication and the data collection directly, which is the correct guidance for a dataset with an accompanying preprint.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: RO-Crate is an established community packaging standard, and its use is corroborated by the errata entry recording RO-Crate metadata corrections in a prior release, which shows it is actually applied rather than merely claimed. The metadata schema is identified by a persistent w3id URI with the conforming class named.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: 'CM4AI project web portal, https://cm4ai.org/, providing project documentation, data release listings, tools and training material'; cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io user documentation; fairscape.github.io with tutorial and installation instructions; page as the repository landing page
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation is available at three levels: the project portal with training material, per-tool user documentation on Read the Docs, and an installation tutorial for the AI-readiness framework. These are working entry points for a newcomer rather than a bare repository link.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries using four distinct relationship_type values, is_new_version_of for the four prior CM4AI releases, is_described_by for the CM4AI preprint, is_referenced_by for the perturbation atlas preprint and references for the Nature multimodal cell maps paper
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationship types are used with genuine discrimination rather than one generic label repeated. The distinction between is_described_by for the paper that describes this project and references for a paper whose data the record explicitly states are a separate dataset is exactly the semantic precision the sub-element is looking for, and each entry's note explains what the related item contains.

strengths: Provenance and version tracking are complete and independently verifiable: five releases addressable by DOI with version numbers, a typed is_new_version_of lineage back to May 2024, a stated quarterly update cadence with a November 2026 end date, and both source cell lines identified by Cellosaurus RRID with their biological origin and third-party access terms.

Source conflicts are surfaced and adjudicated rather than smoothed over. The record documents the 563 versus 464 protein-count disagreement between releases and states which source ranking decided it, notes that the June 2026 image archives carry different MD5 checksums from the October 2025 ones and therefore refuses to carry over their description, records a disputed author affiliation with the tier rule that resolved it, and flags that its own size total disagrees with the project portal by three orders of magnitude.

Ethical documentation is scoped correctly to a dataset with no human participants: two named ethics leads with ORCIDs and working contacts, a Data Governance Committee with a named contact and an access review process, a de-identification basis grounded in commercial cell-line sourcing, and a source_caveat separating the Dataverse field label from the preprint's differently named committee.

Funding and attribution are precise and validated: two structurally valid NIH award numbers with RePORTER corroboration including application ID and project period, release-level funding separated from project-level funding, and 45 creators with 37 ORCIDs, affiliations throughout, and DOI-fragment identifiers minted for those without ORCIDs.

Internal arithmetic is exact and self-checking. The five collection file counts sum to the recorded total of 10 and the five collection byte totals sum to the recorded total_size_bytes to the byte, with a source_caveat stating that both figures are the record's own computation rather than a reported number.

Use guidance covers all three arms with reasoning. The prohibited clinical use carries a stated rationale grounded in the absence of regulatory oversight, and the discouraged use warns specifically that computed cell maps are absent, which is the single most likely misreading of a CM4AI release.
weaknesses: Format documentation stops at the ZIP container. All ten files are recorded as format ZIP with media_type application/zip and nothing states what formats the archives contain, nor is character encoding given anywhere, so a reuser cannot determine whether the mass-spectrometry archives hold mzML, the perturb-seq archive holds MTX or FASTQ, or the 12.6 GB of images are OME-TIFF or PNG.

No variable-level metadata exists anywhere in the record. The variables slot is absent and the only structural typing is at instance level through ontology CURIEs, leaving the tabular SEC-MS, AP-MS and perturb-seq components without any data dictionary.

Processing is undocumented for data that necessarily underwent it. All six preprocessing, cleaning, labeling, annotation, machine-annotation and imputation slots are empty, and the detailed MuSIC pipeline description in notes is explicitly scoped out as project tooling not applied to this release, leaving the instrument-to-archive path unstated for all four modalities.

Data-level quality reporting is absent. The anomalies, sampling_strategies and missing_data_documentation slots are all empty, and no outliers, failed runs, batch effects or quality-control outcomes are reported for any modality.

Instance counts are missing in scientific units. File counts and byte sizes are exact, but the instances block names three measurement types with no count of images, interactions, guides or cells, so a reuser cannot size the data in the terms that matter for analysis planning.

The errata entry contains a self-contradiction, naming the June 2025 release as a revision of 'the preceding June 2025 release' where the record's own related_datasets identify the antecedent as the March 2025 release.

Bias coverage is narrow. A single representation bias is recorded, correctly typed and well reasoned, but future_use_impacts is absent so no anticipated downstream social impact is stated, and no other bias category is considered.
The publisher slot carries a dataset landing-page URL byte-identical to page rather than naming the publishing organization, so a locator sits where an agent identity belongs.
recommendations: Record the inner data formats per collection alongside the ZIP container, naming the mass-spectrometry, sequencing and imaging formats held in each archive, and state character encoding for the text-based components.
Add variable-level metadata with identifiers and descriptions for the tabular SEC-MS, AP-MS and perturb-seq components, so the archives can be integrated rather than merely downloaded.

Populate preprocessing_strategies and the related processing slots with the instrument-to-archive path for each modality, covering peptide search and quantification for the mass-spectrometry data, alignment, guide assignment and count-matrix construction for perturb-seq, and acquisition and export settings for the confocal images, or state explicitly that the archives contain unprocessed instrument output.

Populate anomalies with data-level quality findings such as failed runs, dropped conditions, missing replicates and per-modality coverage holes, and record the sampling strategy behind the chosen conditions and guide library.

Add instance counts in scientific units to the instances block, giving the number of images, interaction measurements, targeted genes and profiled cells per modality, with the same source_caveat discipline already applied to the file totals.
Correct the errata entry to name the March 2025 release as the antecedent of the June 2025 revision, matching the record's own related_datasets notes.
Broaden known_biases beyond the single representation bias and populate future_use_impacts with anticipated downstream effects of training models on two cell lines.
Set publisher to 'University of Virginia Dataverse' and leave the landing-page URL in page, so the slot carries an agent identity rather than a duplicate locator.

metadata.independence_note: No file under data/evaluation_llm/ was opened at any point during this evaluation, including sibling evaluations of the same project or label (#1061). The JSON structure was taken entirely from the agent definition's Output Format section.
metadata.applicability_note: Element 4 was resolved per sub-element rather than once for the element (#1060). Sub-elements 1 and 2 carry the governance disjunct and were scored on the strength of the confidentiality embargo, the commercial-licence restriction and the Data Governance Committee, all evidenced from fields outside Element 4. Sub-elements 3, 4 and 5 are gated on the human-subject condition alone, which is not met, and governance structures are explicitly not a participant signal, so those three are excluded from the denominator. regulatory_restrictions was read as a record that no restriction applies and was not counted as a constraint.
